### MS1 · step 16b — Word syntax errors in Bison's terms and recover where LilyPond does

- **Commits:** the one that adds this entry, feat(engine): word syntax
  errors in Bison's terms and recover where LilyPond does.
- **Built:** P2's second part in `crates/parser`:
  - `bison.rs`:
    - the display names, moved from `lexer.rs`;
    - `syntax error, unexpected X`, with `, expecting A or B …` where
      Bison lists what could follow;
    - the expected set of each error point that has four tokens or fewer.
      These are `'{'` after `\header` and `\score`, `'.' or '='` after an
      assignment's name, `\header` after its `=`, `'}'` in a score's body,
      and the four of `mode_changing_head`. Every other point lists
      nothing.

    The sets come from the states of 2.26.0's `parser.yy` in `bison
    --report=state`. They include the default reductions that an
    unexpected token sets off before Bison detects the error. That is why
    `title = }` expects `\header` (case 03): `}` reduces
    `header_modification`'s empty mid-rule action.
  - `recover.rs`, Bison's recovery in the recursive descent:
    - **Where it recovers.** A `SyntaxError` returns to the innermost
      production with an `error` rule: `music_list`, `score_body` or
      `lilypond`. `resync` there discards tokens until one can follow.
    - **`yyerrstatus`.** An error with no token shifted since the last one
      discards its token. No error is reported until three tokens are
      shifted.
    - **Aborts.** The end of input aborts the parse anywhere but toplevel,
      and no diagnostic follows it.
    - **`Unfinished main input`.** It is reported at the end of input while
      `\notemode` or `\markup` left their lexer mode pushed after an error.
    - **`errors found, ignoring music expression`.** `music-check-error`
      and `Score::set_music` report it for toplevel music and a score's
      first music. It comes after the next token is lexed, where Bison
      reduces those rules.
  - `notes.rs`:
    - `reverse_music_list`'s `Unattached <Event>` when a list closes. A run
      of post-events attaches to the music before it, if that music takes
      them (`add_post_events`), and otherwise the run's first one is
      reported. A run that opens a list is reported whole. A run that ends
      a list becomes an event chord, which takes the next run;
    - `\notemode` and its braced or `<< >>` music (`mode_changed_music`);
    - music lists recover through `resync`.
  - `lib.rs`:
    - toplevel `name = value` (`assignment`), shared with `\header`'s
      body. Its value is a string, a word, a number or music. It is not
      defined anywhere until P3;
    - `\score { … }` with music items:
      - `Missing music in \score` (with no location);
      - `Spurious expression in \score`;
      - `score_body error`;
      - an error inside an item recovers at toplevel, as Bison does,
        because `score_body`'s error state exists only once the items are
        reduced.
  - `syntax.rs`: `Assignment`, `Value`, and the items `Assignment` and
    `Score`. A header's fields are `Assignment`s.
  - `tests/p2_errors.rs`, 8 tests. Every expected message in them was
    printed by LilyPond 2.26.0 for the same input. They cover:
    - the expected sets;
    - a score's body;
    - the three tokens;
    - recovery in music lists;
    - aborts and `Unfinished main input`;
    - `errors found`;
    - `Unattached`, in 8 forms;
    - assignments.
- **Gate:** `c0-cases.test.mjs` has 08, 09, 12 and 30 in `CASES` under P2:

  - **Recovery resumes only at what P2 parses.** After an error, toplevel
    takes music, `\header`, `\markup`, `\score`, `\notemode` and an
    assignment's name, and a music list takes what starts P2's music.
    Bison also resumes at constructs not parsed yet: `#`, `\paper` and
    `\book` at toplevel, and `\markup` in music. Until their steps, those
    are discarded there, and in music `\markup` is a syntax error.
  - **`Unattached` is reported, not done.** The syntax keeps post-events
    as a list's elements. Attaching them is the music value's work.
  - **One `Error` element per recovery.** Bison adds a `music_list error`
    element for each token it discards. Nothing reads the count.
  - **Only `\notemode` and `\markup` count as pushed modes.** The other
    mode switches come with their steps (P7, P9, P10).
  - **Bison 3.8.2 was installed with Homebrew,** keg-only (macOS has 2.3,

### MS1 · step 17a — Evaluate embedded forms at their spans and collect on demand

- **Commits:** the one that adds this entry, feat(engine): evaluate
  embedded forms at their spans and collect on demand.
- **Built:** the interpreter's part of P3 and P4, with no corpus case:
  - `vm.rs`:
    - `Source`, the text a datum was read from as Guile's port sees it:
      the file's name, and the line and column at a byte offset. LilyPond
      sets the score's port to the form's line and to its column less one
      (`parse-scm.cc`). `Source::new` is a whole text from line 0, column 0,
      as `eval_text` and `read` from a string port use it;
    - `Vm::eval_at(read, source, location)`, LilyPond's evaluation of a
      `#` or `$` form:
      - `(*location*)` gives `location` while the form runs, and the value
        before is back afterwards, after an error too, as
        `scm_c_with_fluid` binds it. The value before is rooted meanwhile;
      - psyntax's errors are placed by the reader's spans from `source`,
        so `where` has the score's file, line and column;
    - `Vm::read_error(e, source)`, public now: a read error placed in
      `source`, as case 21's Guile line is;
    - `(gc)` collects at once with the VM's roots, in the call path beside
      `apply` and `eval`.
  - `prims.rs`: `gc` (Guile's, no arguments, unspecified) is primitive 3.
    `apply`, `eval`, `primitive-eval` and `gc` are the first four, so one
    comparison tells the VM's own from the others. `PRIMITIVE_EVAL` is
    gone: it is the index after `EVAL`.
  - `expand.rs`: `(lily curried-definitions)`' `define`, `define*`,
    `define-public` and `define*-public` fail as the file's `syntax-case`
    does when a form fits none of its patterns: `source expression failed
    to match any pattern` at the form, with its place. They passed such
    forms to Guile's own keyword, which gives no place and takes `(define
    x)`. LilyPond 2.26.0 rejects `#(define x)` with `d.ly:2:0:`. The spans
    test found this: a score's module uses `(lily curried-definitions)`.
  - `crates/spike/src/lib.rs`: `lsb_collect`, which evaluates `(gc)`, so
    `lsb_stats` gives that collection's milliseconds and the bytes live
    after it.
  - `scheme-page.js`: after each restore of `scheme.image`, `lsb_collect`.
    The result's `image` has `longestPauseMs`, `allPauseMs` and

  - `tests/spans.rs`, 4 tests. Every expected text was printed by

- **Commits:** the one that adds this entry, feat(engine): classify \name

      parse has a module of its own. The values of identifier tokens are
      rooted while the parse lasts;

      `MUSIC_FUNCTION`, `EVENT_FUNCTION` or `SCM_FUNCTION`, by the result
      predicate its header names. Then numbers, held music and events,
      held pitches, alists whose first key is a `key?` (`LOOKUP_IDENTIFIER`),

      one post-event or a `PostEvents`' events, a pitch), held as 16a's
      syntax in a foreign object until the music-value answer;
    - the `Scopes` trait, which the lexer asks; `NoScopes` is an empty
      module.

    `scan_shorthand` look a name up after the keywords, and only an unbound
    one is an unknown command or an undefined shorthand. `Lexer::next_in`
    takes the scopes; `Lexer::next` has none.
  - `assign.rs`:
    - `assignment`: `name = value`, `"name" = value`, `name.path = value`
      with `.` and `,` (`property_path`), and `set_identifier`, which
      defines into the innermost scope, into a nested alist for a path
      (`nested_create_alist`, `nested_property_alist`), and warns `identifier
      name is a keyword` with no location;
    - `identifier_init` for strings, words, `UNSIGNED`, `REAL`, `-` and a
      number, `FRACTION`s, symbol lists (`foo.bar`, `"foo".bar`, `4.x`),
      post-events, music, pitches with nothing that makes them notes, and
      `\name`s of every kind but functions and books;
    - `lookup`: `\name.key` on an alist (`nested_property`, `'()` when a key
      is missing) and on a module (`not found`).
    - Bison's timing: an assignment lexes the token after its value before
      it defines, except after a `SCM_IDENTIFIER` and a `FRACTION`. That is
      §5.4's table for P3's values, 16 values measured.
  - `notes.rs`: a `MUSIC_IDENTIFIER` is a copy of its music placed at the

### MS1 · step 17c — Run embedded Scheme from the parser with Bison's timing

- **Commits:** feat(engine): run embedded Scheme from the parser with
  Bison's timing; fix(engine): place a lookup's music at the lookup, from
  the step's verification.
- **Built:** P4 in `crates/parser`:
  - `scheme.rs`, new: `parse-scm.cc` for the parser.
    - `Env::read_form`: the reader at the byte after `#` or `$`, with
      `LilyScan` as the `#{ … #}` callback, which finds where a template
      ends. `#@` and `$@` read the form after the `@` as `(apply values
      form)`. A read error is `Guile signaled an error for the expression
      beginning here` at that byte with Guile's text, and the lexer goes on
      at that byte, as LilyPond's does: case 21's `(` is then a shorthand.
      The end of input after `#` fails the file with no message
      (`error_level_`).
    - `Env::eval_form`: `Vm::eval_at` (17a) in the innermost scope, made
      current while the form runs, with `(*location*)` a `Location` that
      prints `#<location file:line:column>`, as LilyPond's does. An error
      is reported as LilyPond reports it, and the value is unspecified.
    - `Parser::scheme_value`, `eval_scm_token`: a `#` runs when the
      grammar takes its token. Bison shifts a `SCM_TOKEN` and reduces it at
      once (a default reduction), so it runs before the next token is
      lexed. Its values after the first are pushed as `SCM_IDENTIFIER`s.
    - `scheme_keys` (`make_reverse_key_list`) and `scale` (`scale?`,
      `scale->factor`).
  - `lexer.rs`: `#` reads its form and is a `SCM_TOKEN` carrying it. `$`
    reads and runs its form at once, and each value is classified as a
    `\name`'s; an unspecified one gives no token. Extra values wait on
    `push_extra_token`'s stack and come before the input's next token.
    `Lexer::error_level` and `Parse::error_level` are LilyPond's
    `error_level_`. Without scopes (`Lexer::next`), both are returned
    unread, as before.
  - `classify.rs`: `Scopes` gains `read` and `immediate`. `Env` keeps the
    forms read, and defines the 17 shorthands of `declarations-init.ly`
    in each file's module, as `init.ly` does before the file. They are
    stand-ins, `Held` as 17b's values, each with its music type and
    `span-direction` as LilyPond 2.26.0 gives them: 12 post-events (`(`
    is a `SlurEvent` of -1) and 5 music (`|`, `\[`, `\]`, `\~`, `\\`).
  - The grammar's places for Scheme, each checked against LilyPond:
    - toplevel `#`, evaluated and ignored;
    - a header's `#`, ignored, and its `$` (`embedded_scm_active`): a
      module or unspecified, else `bad expression type`;
    - an assignment's `#` value;
    - property paths' and lookups' `#` and `SCM_IDENTIFIER` parts
      (`symbol_list_part`): a key, a string or a list of them, else `not a
      key`;
    - in music, `#` as `music_embedded_backup`: music, a post-event too,
      or `Ignoring non-music expression`;
    - multipliers (`multiplier_scm`): `NUMBER_IDENTIFIER`s, `#` and
      `SCM_IDENTIFIER`s, else `not a multiplier`.
  - The value of a `#` or `$` form keeps the place of its music, as
    LilyPond keeps a music's origin. `\name`, shorthands and `\name.key`
    lookups (`loc_on_copy`) place a copy at the name. The verification
    found that the first commit had lookups keep the place too, and fixed
    it (`v01`).
  - `diag.rs`: what Scheme writes to the error port waits as Guile's
    buffer does. It comes out before Guile's text of an error and at the
    end of the file, and LilyPond's own messages go first. Five inputs
    showed this (`o01`–`o03`, `x16`, `du`).
  - `source.rs`: a `Source` keeps its text as a `String` when it is
    UTF-8, checked once, and else a copy of the valid prefix for the
    reader.
  - `examples/parse.rs`: `--time` prints each file's milliseconds.
- **The scheme crate:** `Vm::set_current_module`; `Heap::values_items`

- **§5.4's table for P4,** measured with LilyPond 2.26.0: whether a `$` on

### MS1 · step 18a — Apply music functions by their signatures

- **Commits:** feat(engine): apply music functions by their signatures.
- **The stop point for music values was reached, and asked.** Case 17
  needs music values in LilyPond's order of calls:
  - defining `\transpose` evaluates `(make-music 'Music)`, the default of
    `define-music-function`'s result;
  - for `c`, `make_music_from_simple` makes a NoteEvent and `ly:pitch?` is
    called on it, then on the pitch;
  - after `"d"`'s error, `ly:music?` is called on `{ c4 }`.

  The user chose a minimal music value over moving N2's frozen music
  forward (D65).
- **Built:**
  - **`crates/music/src/music.rs`, new (D65):**
    - the `Music` and `MusicFunction` foreign types, each with its image
      loader;
    - eleven `ly:` primitives: making music, `ly:music?`, `ly:event?`,
      properties, deep copies, and making and reading music functions;
    - `define-music-types.scm`'s `make-music`, over a `%music-properties`
      table of each type's name and `types`. `define_music_types` reads
      that table from the file as data, nothing evaluated: 131 types.
  - **`crates/parser`, P5 part 1:**
    - `function.rs`, new: what LilyPond's `ly-syntax-constructors.scm` and
      `parser.yy` do around a call.
      - `function_call` reads a function's signature from its
        `MusicFunction`, then its arguments.
      - `music-function` applies the function when every argument was
        good, and checks the result with the signature's first predicate.
        A result that fails is `music function cannot return …`, worded
        as `value->lily-string` words it. The value is then the
        signature's fallback, copied if it is music.
      - `argument-error` gives `wrong type for argument N.  Expecting X,
        found Y`. X is `type-name`'s, and Y is `music->make-music`'s,
        written. Both are called in `(lily)` as LilyPond calls them.
      - `make_music_from_simple`, and music values made from the syntax.
        Their properties are in the order LilyPond's actions set them, the
        last set first.
      - `define_type_names`: `lily.scm`'s `type-p-name-alist`, built from
        its five lists as data, of the predicates `(lily)` has.
    - `args.rs`, new: `parser.yy`'s 96 argument productions as one loop
      over the parameters, left to right.
      - A parameter is read in one of three contexts: mandatory; optional
        with a mandatory one after its run (the backup rules); optional at
        the end (the nonbackup rules).
      - The readings by first token, each a predicate call in the rules'
        order:
        - `#`, `SCM_ARG`, a fraction, a lookup, music and calls
          (`embedded_scm_arg`);
        - a `SCM_IDENTIFIER`, a `STRING` or a `SYMBOL`
          (`try_string_variants`, `try_word_variants`, symbol lists with
          more parts after `.` and `,`, the lyric reading);
        - a pitch (the note of the default duration, then
          `pitch_or_music`);
        - an `UNSIGNED` (a number with its unit, `(n)`, a duration, the
          note of a duration);
        - `REAL` and `NUMBER_IDENTIFIER`, `-` with a number (the
          `FingeringEvent` reading), and post-events.
      - A predicate that rejects a mandatory argument is called once more
        (`check_scheme_arg`), and the error is placed where LilyPond
        places it.
      - `\default` gives a parameter and the rest of its run their
        defaults.
      - A token no argument starts with is `syntax error, unexpected X,
        expecting \header`, or `expecting (backed-up?)` while an optional
        parameter could still back up. These are Bison's sets, as
        `bison.rs` gives `ARGUMENT` and `BACKED_UP`.
    - `cursor.rs`, new: Bison's `BACKUP`. A rejected optional argument
      goes back in front of the lexer's next token as one cached token that
      carries its value:
      - `SCM_ARG` (`Tok::ScmArg`), `STRING`, `PITCH_IDENTIFIER`,
        `EVENT_IDENTIFIER`, `UNSIGNED` (after `-` too), or
        `NUMBER_IDENTIFIER`;
      - so Scheme is not run again, music is not parsed again and no error
        is reported twice.

      `REPARSE` needs no token: the reading goes on from what it read.
    - The grammar's places for calls:
      - a music function's call is `composite_music`, in music, at
        toplevel and as a value;
      - a Scheme function's is `embedded_scm`: at toplevel (`bad
        expression type`), in music (`Ignoring non-music expression`) and
        as a value;
      - an event function's is a post-event, with a direction or none.
      - A result, and a music value that a `\name` or a `#` form gives,
        is `MusicKind::Value`, or `PostEventKind::Value` for a post-event.
        Its type decides whether it takes post-events and what
        `Unattached` names.
    - `classify.rs`: a music function by its result's predicate, compared
      with `ly:music?` and `ly:event?` by identity (D65); a music value as
      `MUSIC_IDENTIFIER` or `EVENT_IDENTIFIER`.
    - The lexer's `push_token`, `add_string`, `pitch_name` and
      `name_of_pitch`. A pitch table keeps each name's place in the file,
      for `note-name->lily-string`'s `rassoc`.
  - **The scheme crate:** `Vm::define_primitives` exports what it
    defines, as `LY_DEFINE` does (D65). A file's module did not see N1's
    `ly:` functions before: step 17c timed `#(ly:make-moment 1/4)` as an

### MS1 · step 18b — Parse output blocks and number expressions

- **Commits:** feat(engine): parse output blocks and number expressions.
- **No stop point:** neither case needed a music value beyond D65's.
- **Built (`crates/parser`, P5 part 2):**
  - **`output_def.rs`, new.** `header_block`, `header_modification`,
    `score_block`, `book_block`, `bookpart_block` and `output_def` as
    nested scopes, with the placement rules of their actions:
    - **Scopes.** `Env` gains `add_scope` and `remove_scope`. A scope's
      module uses `(guile)`, `(lily)` and the scopes around it, the
      innermost searched first. Assignments define into it and forms run
      in it. After a syntax error that a block does not recover from, its
      scope stays, as LilyPond leaves it.
    - **Output definitions.** Each is a copy of what `get_paper`,
      `get_layout` or `get_midi` find: the top of a book's `$papers`, or
      the kind's default, of the kind it is copied for. The body is lexed
      in initial mode (`push_initial_state`, counted in `pushed`, so `\paper
      x` gives `Unfinished main input`). An output definition as the
      body's first item replaces it; anywhere else it is `bad expression
      type`. A toplevel one becomes `$defaultpaper`, `$defaultlayout` or
      `$defaultmidi`, and so does one given as Scheme at toplevel.
    - **Headers.** A toplevel `\header` is a copy of `$defaultheader`
      that replaces it. A book's, a part's and a score's header is theirs,
      and a header as a value is a new module. A module given as Scheme is
      copied into the header (`ly_module_copy`).
    - **Scores.** `score_items`' action: the first music, or a score given
      as Scheme, is the score's. Later music or values are `Spurious
      expression in \score`, and a `\paper` is `\paper cannot be used in
      \score, use \layout instead` (case 11). Headers are the score's,
      before its music too. `Missing music in \score` and `score_body
      error` are 16b's.
    - **Books and parts.** `init_papers`, `push_paper`, `set_paper` and
      `pop_paper` for a book; `$current-book` and `$current-bookpart`;
      `need \paper for paper block`; a `BOOK_IDENTIFIER` first in the body
      takes the book's place; a part in a part and a book in a book are
      syntax errors. Their `error` rules resume at the next item or `}`.
    - **Values.** `Score`, `Book` and `OutputDef` are foreign values with
      no more in them than these rules read. A `Book` is a
      `BOOK_IDENTIFIER`. The handlers that LilyPond hands blocks to
      (`toplevel-score-handler`, `book-music-handler`, …) are not called.
    - **Defaults.** `define_defaults` puts `$defaultpaper`,
      `$defaultlayout` and `$defaultmidi` into each file's module, each
      with its `output-def-kind`. The paper and the layout have
      `paper-defaults-init.ly`'s units (`mm cm in pt bp`); the midi has
      none. These are stand-ins until the init files run, as the
      shorthands are.
  - **`number.rs`, new:** `number_expression`, `number_term`,
    `number_factor` and `bare_number` as an assignment's value:
    - `+` and `-` left to right, and one `*` or `/` a term, so `2 * 3 * 4`
      is a syntax error at the second `*`;
    - unary `-`, and units after an `UNSIGNED` or a `REAL`;
    - `expecting UNSIGNED or NUMBER_IDENTIFIER or REAL or '-'` where a
      factor is missing (`bison.rs`'s `NUMBER_FACTOR`).

    `args.rs`'s `number_value` and `bare_number` moved here.
  - **`Parser::base`:** the mode a block's own tokens are lexed in,
    initial in an output definition and notes elsewhere. `assign.rs`'s
    assignments, values, property paths and lookups use it. `in_notes`
    reads music, post-events and calls in notes mode, from the lookahead
    on. The lookahead keeps the kind it was lexed with, as Bison's does
    when the lexer's state changes after it.
  - **`assignment` always defines.** A header's fields now go into the
    header's module.
  - **`notes.rs`:** `embedded_scm` is split into `embedded_scm_value` and
    `scheme_music`, so a score sees a value before it is taken as music.
  - **`syntax.rs`:** `ItemKind::Score`, `Book`, `BookPart` and
    `OutputDef(OutputKind, …)` hold their items; `Value::Block` is a block
    as a value.
- **The scheme crate:** `Vm::module_use` (`module-use!`, which

The engine has a fourth crate of its own, `core` (`lily_engine_core`,
K2), which exports 08 §4.2's ABI beside the bench's `lsb_*` and the
parser's `lsp_*`, holds the image writer and the needs loop, and is
charged to the driver's row; the spike is no longer linked. The music
crate holds frozen music, contexts and the translator framework (D73,
D79), N4's iterators, N6 and N7. The studio's driver (`packages/studio/src/web/engine/`)
runs the engine unchanged in its ABI; its protocol carries files as bytes
since step 41a (D102). The tools gained the reference captures (tokens,
trees, traces) and C1's comparisons in `tools/compare/`, and the
harness `translate.html` and `restore.html`. The four crates' source is
53,701 non-blank lines at 6ebcddd (`scheme` 21,730, `music` 17,279,
`parser` 13,422, `core` 1,270), against 28,109 at MS1's close (6ea5d19:
19,762 + 1,821 + 6,526); the crates' Rust tests 21,426 (13,858 by the
same count at MS1's close). The diff from 6ea5d19 to 6ebcddd is 171
files, +52,581 / −1,971 lines, docs included (`git diff --shortstat`;
all of these in step 42's `audit-crate-lines.txt`).

### Deviations from the roadmap

- **N2 replaced D65's minimal music value behind the same face** (D67),
  and the C++ callbacks of later milestones are named placeholders (D67),
  with only what MS2's gate needs ported ahead: `Grace_engraver` whole,
  which makes no grobs (D94), `Repeat_acknowledge_engraver` (D96), and
  the parts of seven slur, tie and beam translators that set the melisma
  properties (D98).
- **Contexts and the translator framework are modules of `crates/music`**
  (D73, D79), with LilyPond's primitives as their only Scheme face.
- **The parts on demand** (`chords`, `display`, `fretted`, `diagrams`,
  `partcombine`, `modal`) load from source on their trigger through
  stubs (D74, D76), asked of the host through `lily_needs` (D80), a
  part's files at one stop (D89); `chords` and `fretted` init files are
  snapshotted in the image (D78). `partcombine`'s GOOPS is not there, so
  `\partCombine`, `\autoChange` and `\addQuote` wait.
- **LilyPond's regular expressions match as PCRE in Rust** (D81), and the
  stencil and Bézier primitives `diagrams` runs at load were ported then.
- **Templates run LilyPond's own `parser-ly-from-scheme.scm`**, the
  parser a host of the interpreter (D92); `\etc` uses
  `ly-syntax-constructors.scm`'s constructors (D93). P12's productions
  `syntax.ly` reaches came forward from MS8; the rest of P12 stays there.
- **Every compile translates its `\layout`s** (D99), so translation timed
  since step 40 is more than part 3 timed (T29 2.24 times natively);
  LilyPond's `stderr` of T03 needs it.
- **"The translation traces of all 30" is read as each score's own**
  (D100): T23's incipits, translated by layout from inside markup, are
  MS3's.
- **K2's corpus test is a studio test** over the engine's build read as
  files (D101), and **the page↔engine protocol carries files as bytes**
  (D102, the user's answer at step 41), so case 06's Latin-1 reaches the
  engine as LilyPond reads it; `outcomeOf` takes entry 0 of the playback
  map (D103). 08 §4.2's ABI is unchanged.
- **The tablet was run once in MS2** (part 3's close, step 28); parts 1
  and 2 skipped it at the user's word, and part 4's close ran an Android
  emulator with Chrome in its place (the user away). Throttled desktop
  Chromium stood in for its first restore.
- **D88:** a device miss of a Must by more than twice gets a step in the
  next part. It gave part 4 steps 30 and 31.
- 08 §4.1–§4.2's text still says the page sends texts (D102).

The shares sum to 24,000–38,000, README §5.1's re-estimate. MS1's parts
ran 1.8–3.3 times their shares of the old estimate; these shares already
carry R12's factor. Each closing step reports its part's lines against
its share, and the next split re-estimates the parts left. A split cuts any step that looks bigger than one session (two to
three hours, at most about 2,500 lines), as MS1's 10a/10b, 12a/12b and
16a–18b were.

**Why this order.**

- **The tools come first** (part 1, step 1), as MS0's step 4 captured
  before M1. Every MS2 step is checked against LilyPond's music trees, its
  `-ddebug-parser` token sequence or 04 Appendix A's translation trace, and
  none of these exists yet. The trace of 04 Appendix A (`c4.ly`'s `trace`
  mode) is captured in part 3, the first part that translates.
- **N2 before P6.** P6's operations become frozen `PropertySet`,
  `OverrideProperty` and `ContextSpeccedMusic`, and its gate compares music
  trees, so frozen music must exist first.
- **K2 and the whole init share part 2.** The image of the whole init is
  what `lily_start` restores, and K2 moves the image writer out of the
  spike, so the two change the same files. The init needs P6 (part 1;
  `property-init.ly`, `context-mods-init.ly`, `engraver-init.ly`), P7
  (`toc-init.ly` and the markup definitions) and N3's context definitions
  (`engraver-init.ly`, `performer-init.ly`), so they come with or before
  it.
- **The 14 scores of part 3** are those N4 makes iterable (04 §13: T01,
  T03, T05, T06, T08, T13–T19, T21, T28, T29) less T28, which needs
  P11's includes and templates. They need P9 (T17, T19, T29) and P10 (T05,
  T06, T21), so P9 and P10 come in part 3. T19 includes `articulate.ly`
  and T21 `example-header.ily`, so **part 3 also takes `\include` of a
  string through the search path** from P11; `\name` and Scheme includes,
  templates and partial functions stay in part 4.
- **Part 4 is what only the last scores and `syntax.ly` need:** lyrics
  (P8, N7: T20, T23 and the scores with `\addlyrics`), grace notes and
  `\change` (N6: T09, T11, T12, T22, T25–T27), volta repeats (N7), and P11's
  templates. `syntax.ly` uses a few of P12's productions (`c4*#1`, a
  `*#scheme` multiplier; `\markuplist` with a command), which part 4
  brings forward from MS8; the rest of P12 stays there.

**What part 2's init needs from later parts.** Run at load, the init
files reach a little of parts 3 and 4: `ancient-init.ly` defines `IJ =
\lyricmode { Ĳ }` and three more (P8), and `property-init.ly` and
`chord-repetition-init.ly` hold `#{ … #}` in function bodies, which P4
reads with their extent and P11 parses when the function is called. Part
2 brings forward what runs at load (the lyric syllables at least) and
lists anything else by running the init with each missing construct
reported. Templates in function bodies wait for part 4; until then a call
of such a function is recorded, not failed silently.

**The image (R2).** MS1 extrapolated 528.5 KB brotli against 420. Part 1's
closing step extrapolates it again with frozen music saved in it (step
3). Part 2 writes the whole init and measures it: no extrapolation from
then on. If part 2 measures it over 420, that is a budget miss and
recorded as MS1's were; a miss by more than twice (840 KB) is reported to
the user before part 3 is split. R2's leads (the 9-byte instructions,
README §8's documentation strings out, init data as generated Rust tables)
get no step unless the user asks for one.

of the part named, and again by every later closing step:

Simulator (the stand-in for the iPhone), and the Android tablet (the
stand-in for the A15-class phone): woken with `adb shell svc power stayon
true`, unlocked with Silk in front, Silk's
`cpuset` checked to be `/top-app`, and `stayon` set back to `false`
afterwards. The real phones are listed by hand. From part 2 the harness
also loads the core through K2's ABI.

**MS1's six misses** stay recorded and get no step of their own (the
user's word at this split). The closing steps measure them again: 341.2 ns
per application; b5's 13.4–13.7 ms pause; the image at 528.5 KB brotli
extrapolated (measured from part 2); the tablet's first restore in a fresh
worker at 52.8–81.6 ms; the warm restore extrapolated to 64–69 ms
(measured from part 2); one first collection of 13.0 ms in a fresh worker.

**Stop points the plan already sees.** A step that reaches one stops and
asks (PLAN-RUN §3):

- **D65's face** (part 1, steps 2–3). Frozen music keeps the face of
  `ly:make-music`, `ly:music-property`, `ly:music-set-property!`,
  `ly:music-mutable-properties`, `ly:music-deep-copy` and `make-music`. If
  a primitive must behave differently from D65's to match LilyPond, the
  step stops.
- **C++ callbacks of later milestones** (every part). A music type's
  callbacks that belong to layout or MIDI (MS3–MS5) are named placeholders
  under a D-number that step 2 records. A step that would implement one
  ahead of its milestone, or a gate item that cannot pass with the
  placeholder, stops.
- **K2's ABI** (part 2). K2 replaces the spike's cdylib as the core; the
  image writer (`examples/bench.rs`), `scheme.image` beside `core.image`,
  and the `lsb_*` and `lsp_*` exports move with it. If 08 §4.2's ABI or
  the studio's driver (`packages/studio/src/web/engine/`, MIT, D56) would
  have to change, or the bench and parser exports cannot stay beside the
  ABI, the step stops. How the engine's tools run the studio's worker in
  Node without reaching into another package is part of this stop point.
- **Module boundaries** (parts 2 and 3). Where contexts (N3) and the
  translator framework (N5, with the Scheme translators and the playback
  map's performer) live, in `crates/music` or crates of their own, and
  what they expose to Scheme. **Part 2's split asks the user about
  contexts, and part 3's split about the translator framework,** before
  writing the step lines. Part 2's split also asks how 03 §6's parts on
  demand (`chords`, `display`, `fretted`, `diagrams`, `partcombine`,
  `modal`) are present before S6 and K4: loaded into the image and charged
  apart from the core's 420 KB, or loaded from source on their trigger.
  T05 (`chords`), T19 (`display`, through `articulate.ly`), T22 (`fretted`)
  and T29 (`diagrams`, `harp-pedals`) need them for C1.

**`PARTS` in `scripts/sizes.mjs`.** A step that creates a crate adds it to
its README §4.1 part in the same commit. K2's core crate goes under
*Driver, ABI, diagnostics, Rust runtime*; contexts and translators under
*Music model*, wherever part 2's and part 3's answers put them. Each
closing step checks that no engine crate's code is charged to the runtime
row or an unbudgeted one, and that every export prefix (`lily_*`, `lsb_*`,
`lsp_*` and K2's) is charged to the core's row.

Between the parts, by hand:

- the device runs that the closing step lists;
- the answers to the stop points above that the next split asks;
- then Mother's split of the next part, from this plan and the closing
  step's *Next*.

#### Part 2: K2's core, `lily.scm`'s Scheme files, P7, N3's definitions, the whole init

**The answers this split asked** (*Stop points*), given by the user at
the split:

- **Where contexts live: D73.** They are a module of `crates/music`
  (`context_def.rs` in part 2, the instances in part 3), charged to
  *Music model* with the crate, so `PARTS` gets no new row. Their Scheme
  face is LilyPond's own primitives and nothing else.
- **How the parts on demand are present before S6 and K4: D74.** They load
  from source on their trigger and are not in the image, so R2's 420 KB is
  measured on the core alone. Until a part loads, every name it defines is
  a stub in the core, and the init stores or calls stubs without forcing
  them. `chord-modifiers-init.ly` runs when `chords` loads, and
  `predefined-fretboards-init.ly` and `string-tunings-init.ly` when
  `fretted` loads. `display-lily` comes with `display`. So part 2's gate
  reads "`declarations-init.ly` with the 21 files it includes" as the 18
  in the image and those three run when their parts load.

#### Part 3: N3's instances, N4, N5, P9, P10: C1 on 14 scores

**The answer this split asked** (*Stop points*), given by the user at the
split:

- **Where the translator framework lives: D79.** It is a module of
  `crates/music`, beside D73's contexts and N4's iterators: translator
  classes, groups, listeners, acknowledgers, the timestep protocol,
  `Timing_translator`, the Scheme translators and the playback map's
  performer. It is charged to *Music model* with the crate, so `PARTS`
  gets no new row. Its Scheme face is LilyPond's own primitives and
  nothing else. The playback map leaves through the core's ABI as
  `<name>.timing.json`.

**The re-estimate** (R12). Part 1 came in at 6,116 lines (1.02 times its
low end) and part 2 at 4,872 (0.70 times), since `lily.scm`'s files loaded
as they are. Part 3 is mostly models (N3's instances, N4, N5), which part
1's rate fits, and partly grammar and loading (P9, P10, the needs loop),
which part 2's fits:

**How the gate reads.**

- **"Translation traces per context and timestep equal 04 Appendix A's"**
  is read as 04 §13 checks its steps: the events each context hears, per
  timestep (`c4.ly`'s `E` lines, with its `P` lines), in the `\layout`
  translation that `c4.ly` records, and the context properties at bar
  starts (its `S` lines). Step 22's capture writes `S` lines one property
  at a time instead of hashed. A property set by an engraver of chapter
  05 (MS3) is recorded by name, not failed. The `G` lines (grobs
  announced) are MS3's, since part 3 makes no grobs.
- **C1** is `score.mjs`'s Dice of the playback map's events against the
  MS0 capture's `.timing.json`. The capture gives every book a `\midi`
  performance (`capture.ly`), and the engine does the same.

**Placed here, beyond the parts table.**

- **`ly:regex-exec`** (step 20): T02, T06, T21 and T29 use `\clef`, and
  so do T11, T12, T22 and T27, whose trees stop there.
- **The parts on demand that the 14 trigger:** `display` through T19's
  `articulate.ly` (step 19), `diagrams` through T29's `\harp-pedal` (step
  20; `ly:bezier-extract` a D67 placeholder if it is called), `chords`
  through T05's chord mode (step 21). In wasm they need the core's part
  source (D74's `lily_put` and `lily_needs`, step 19).
- **The 16 default Scheme engravers stay Scheme in part 3.** 04 §13 puts
  their move to Rust in N5. They make grobs, which no part 3 gate checks,
  and 04 §13 says N5 needs no engraver beyond `Timing_translator` for C1.
  So step 26 runs `scheme-engravers.scm`'s translators as Scheme
  translators, and their port to Rust waits for MS3, where their grobs
  are compared.
- **Left by part 2 and not placed here:** a file's `define` of an init
  variable shadowing it, variable objects, an output definition's parent,
  and init origins in diagnostics. A step that reaches one does it or
  records it. Templates, `\name` and Scheme includes and partial functions
  stay in part 4 (P11).
- **The budgets first measured in part 3:** the first full parse of T02
  (40 / 10 ms) and T29 (150 / 80 ms), and the translation of a whole score
  (S 60 / 20 ms, L 250 / 100 ms) on its 14 scores, natively by steps 20
  and 27, and on the devices by step 28 through a harness page that step
  27 adds; the music model's row with N4 and N5.
- **The Android tablet** is run by step 28, since steps 8 and 17 skipped it
  at the user's word. MS1's ratios extrapolate its first restore in a
  fresh worker and its first collection to 2–3 times their Must.

  and `S` lines as step 22 reads them. A property set by a translator of
  chapter 05 or 07 is recorded by name; the `G` lines are MS3's.

  scores and the 30 cases are compiled by the studio's own driver in
  Node, over the built `core.wasm` and `core.image`. The page's side
  answers `needs-file` from disk, the score's directory and `<datadir>`.
  Each output equals the native core's, and the outputs are judged by
  chapter 00's comparator (C1 on the 30, C0 on T03 and the cases).

### MS2 · step 1 — Capture LilyPond's music trees and parser token traces as references

- **Commits:** feat(engine): capture LilyPond's token sequences and music
  trees as references; fix(engine): include strings with
  ly:parser-include-string for T16's tokens.
- **Built:**
  - **`tools/compare/music.ly`**, a settings file after 04 Appendix A's
    `c4.ly` (census mode's walk): its `toplevel-book-handler` writes each
    score's music to `MUSIC_OUT` as the handler gets it and handles the book
    no further. One line per node (`NoteEvent @file.ly:16:4-16:6`, the
    origin's file base name, first and last line and column from
    `ly:input-both-locations`), its mutable properties below it sorted by
    name, music and lists of music nested, other values written with
    procedures by name, context mods by their lists, unpure-pure containers
    by their parts and Guile's addresses taken out; a node met again is
    written as `= Name @origin`.
  - **`tools/compare/tokens.mjs`** reads Bison's `-ddebug-parser` trace
    into the tokens Bison read, one a line by their names in Bison's
    messages (`\header`, `'{'`, `NOTENAME_PITCH`, `scheme?`, `end of
    input`). The trace starts at `\maininput`, so the first token of the
    main file is the one whose read was in progress; it ends with the main
    file's parse, before `init.ly`'s tail. Parses inside it (`#{ … #}`) are
    indented a level. A token the parser pushed back (the value after
    `(reparsed?)` or `(backed-up?)`, and the lookahead pushed back with it,
    found from the lookahead Bison had not shifted) is marked `^`. The
    compare is of the tokens the lexer gave unless `--full`: the `^` tokens
    and `(reparsed?)`, `(backed-up?)` left out.
  - **`tools/compare/music.mjs`** compares two dumps line by line and
    reports the first difference with its path (`score 1 ›
    SequentialMusic @… › elements › BarEvent @… › bar-type`).
  - **`capture.mjs --parse`** writes `<corpus>/parse/<ID>/` (never
    committed): `tokens.txt`, `music.txt`, `stderr.txt` without the trace
    and `capture.json`, for T01–T30, `syntax` and `init` by default.
    `init` is the parse of `declarations-init.ly` that starts a session:
    `ly:parse-init` never turns the trace on, and a session cannot include
    the init again (`call-after-session used after session start`), so
    `-e` gives `ly:parse-init` a root file that starts with `\maininput`
    (its main file, `<impossible>`, is not found, and lilypond exits 1
    after the parse) and includes `declarations-init.ly`. Each `\include`
    of the init is wrapped in `$` forms of no value, which give no token
    and write `@@ begin <file>` and `@@ end <file>` into the trace; the
    tokens are split there into `init/<file>/tokens.txt` for
    `declarations-init.ly` and each of the 21 files, those a file includes
    with it. So the init files' tokens are classified as at a session's
    start.
  - **The engine's tokens:** `Lexer::record_tokens` records the name of each
    token the parser takes from the lexer, and after a function's token the
    `scheme?`, `optional?` and `EXPECT_NO_MORE_ARGS` that `scan_scm_id`
    pushes (the last parameter's first), from the new
    `Scopes::parameters`. A token `cursor.rs` put back is recorded `^` when
    read again. `parse_tokens` returns them in `Parse::tokens`, and the
    parse example writes them with `--tokens <dir>` to `<name>.tokens`.
  - **`ly:parser-include-string`, brought forward from P11** (the
    verification found T16's tokens unequal without it): Scheme in `(lily)`
    (`define_include_string`, called by `tests/support`'s `load_library`,
    so the image has it) that checks its argument as `LY_ASSERT_TYPE` does
    and keeps it in a box. After each `#` or `$` form runs, the parser
    takes the strings and the lexer reads them next as `<included
    string>`, on a stack of inputs: the end of a string goes back to what
    it interrupted and gives no token. The strings' sources are numbered
    after the main file and copied into `Parse::sources`.
- **Gate:** the step line's items:
  - **The captures:** all 30 scores, `syntax.ly` and the init (9,898
    tokens; the 22 files from 3 to 3,666) in 3.9 s on 5 workers. Two runs
    give the same `tokens.txt` and `music.txt` byte for byte. T03 exits 1
    as it must, and `init` 1 as above. Every score gives one score's tree,
    `syntax.ly` three.
  - **The self-tests:** a sequence and a tree against themselves pass; a
    token changed, dropped or added, and a tree with a node's type, a
    property's name, a value, an origin changed or a property dropped,
    fail where they were changed. Checked on a cut-down trace and fixture
    without LilyPond, and on the captures of T14, T16, the init and
    `music-functions-init.ly` with it.
  - **T14's tokens equal LilyPond's** (26, as the lexer gave them; the
    whole sequence adds `(reparsed?)` and `^SCM_ARG` after `".|:"`), and
    **`music-functions-init.ly`'s 488 equal the init parse's**, the
    engine's final `end of input` aside, which an included file does not
    give. T14's music tree is checked line for line in `music.test.mjs`.
  - **T16's tokens equal LilyPond's** (20), with the included string's.

- **Where the other sequences differ first** (as the lexer gave them):
  T10, T14, T16 and T17 are equal. The others, by what is missing:
  - `\include` (P11; T21, T23, T25, T30, and T01 and T03's `\include` of

  - names that the init's stand-ins do not define yet, lexed as `STRING`

    without LilyPond the table is empty). Each entry holds the type's name,

    `freeze`, which copies frozen music already in it; `thaw` in place;
    digests without `origin`; printing a handle without thawing it;
    `save` and a loader.
  - **`music.rs`:** `Music` is live (D65's, with the whole immutable list)

    `set_mutable_properties`, `is_frozen` and `frozen_node`.
  - **The parser** uses those helpers in place of D65's fields. It freezes

      child's pitch is read without thawing the child, and its

### MS2 · step 10 — Create the core crate with 08 §4.2's ABI and move the image writer into it

- **Commits:** feat(engine): give the engine a core crate behind 08 §4.2's
  ABI (K2).
- **Built:**
  - **`crates/core` (`lily_engine_core`),** a `cdylib` and `rlib` over the
    parser, the Scheme and the music model. `src/lib.rs` holds the
    `Engine`:
    - `lily_start` restores the core's image;
    - `lily_put` keeps source files, `None` when the host has no such file,
      and ignores a module's data, which nothing reads yet;
    - `lily_compile` starts a compile of its root;
    - `lily_step` asks for a root it was not given (2, kind 0). Otherwise
      it parses the root in one step and writes one output, `stderr`, which
      is `Parse::stderr()`. A root answered `null` gives LilyPond's
      `warning: cannot find file:` and `fatal error: failed files:` lines.
      What Scheme wrote to its ports is dropped until step 11's one list.

    `src/abi.rs` is 08 §4.2's nine `lily_*` exports over one `Engine` per
    instance, with `lsb_*` and `lsp_*` beside them as the spike exported
    them. `env.lily_now` is the only import.
  - **The core's image** (`write_image`): `LILYCORE`, the length and text of
    `define-note-names.scm`, then the interpreter's image, byte for byte
    `scheme.image`. The parser needs the pitch names as a `NoteNames`, and
    `define-note-names.scm` loads into the interpreter only in step 12, so
    until then the names travel as text in the image.
  - **Moved from the spike** (`git mv`): `src/bench.rs` (the `lsb_*`
    interpreter) and `examples/bench.rs` (the image writer and the native
    bench). `examples/bench.rs` gained `--write-core-image <scheme.image>
    <define-note-names.scm> <out>`. It prints JSON with its own
    `push_json` and `push_num`, the spike's, so the native lines are
    unchanged. The spike keeps its toy engine and its own `lily_*`, but no
    longer depends on the parser, the Scheme or the music crate.
  - **`scripts/build.mjs`** builds `lily-engine-core` as `core.wasm`.
    `scheme.image` is written as before, and `core.image` beside it by
    `--write-core-image`. Without LilyPond 2.26.0 the build fails, since
    the core cannot start without its image. `CORE=spike` builds the spike
    in its place, with `prelude.scm` as `core.image`, for MS0's harness
    pages (`index.html`, `preview.html`, `l532.mjs`), which need its SVG

### MS2 · step 11 — Write stderr and diagnostics.json from one list and run the 25 cases through the core

- **Commits:** feat(engine): write stderr and diagnostics.json from one
  list, and collect what a compile made (K2).
- **Built:**
  - **One list per compile** (`crates/core/src/diag.rs`, 08 §6). The
    parser now places its diagnostics (`Diagnostics::messages`,
    `Parse::messages`): each `diag::Message` has its file named as the host
    gave it, its line and column counted, and its excerpt, and `failed
    files:` is one of them (`Severity::Fatal`). The core's `List` is those
    messages, or a missing root's two, and writes both outputs:
    - `stderr`, each message as LilyPond prints it, the same bytes as
      `Parse::stderr()`, which now writes the same messages;
    - `diagnostics.json`, the list as `LyDiagnostic[]`: what `parseStderr`
      makes of that stderr. A message starts a diagnostic, and the lines
      after it that start none are its message's, trimmed, empty ones and
      `continuing, cross fingers` dropped, `<…>` files given to the root
      with their place, duplicates and the summary dropped as there.
      Messages carry their place, so their excerpt is never read as a
      line. Text Scheme wrote is read line by line, since a line of it can
      start a message, with `parseHeader`'s two patterns written out in
      Rust.
  - **Warnings in their place among what Scheme wrote to the error port.**
    LilyPond 2.26.0 prints its messages at once and Guile's error port when
    it is flushed (probe below). `force-output` on the error port now
    records how much was flushed (`Cx::flushed`,
    `Vm::take_error_port`), each message of the music crate's `%diagnose`
    records that mark (`%diagnostic-mark`), and the parser's
    `take_scheme_output` (it was `take_diagnostics`, with the errors taken
    before it) puts each message after that much of the text. A programming
    error is now LilyPond's own text (`Diagnostics::raw`) and flushes
    nothing.
  - **`Engine::step` in `compile.rs`,** with two outputs, `stderr` and
    `diagnostics.json`. Scheme's standard output is LilyPond's stdout and
    no output of a compile. `Engine::collect` collects and gives the heap's
    counts, for the tests.
  - **An `Input` names its file** (`crates/music/src/input.rs`): the name the
    host gave, shared by a parse's inputs (`Source::input`), and its first
    byte's line, character and column. It prints as before and answers
    `ly:input-file-line-char-column`, new. A parse takes an `Input`'s span
    only when it has a file of that number and that name
    (`Lexer::span_of`, `Diagnostics::at_input`, `At::Input`); else a
    message at it prints `file:line:column:` without an excerpt, where it
    used to quote whatever file of the parse had its number (D69).
  - **A music function runs with `(*location*)` its call's,** as
    `MAKE_SYNTAX` binds it (`apply_function`); it was `#f` there. With
    Guile's `file-name-separator-string`, `withRelativeDir` gives what
    LilyPond 2.26.0 gives for a file named as it was put: `"./probe.ly"`.
  - **Values unrooted per toplevel item** (`Env::release`). After each item
    the parser unroots what it kept for tokens, except the values of the
    lookahead and of tokens pushed to come next. The file's module is held
    while the parse lasts, and so is each score's music (`Env::hold`); a
    scope's module is kept like any value.
  - **Anonymous modules collected** (`module.rs`, `heap.rs`, `vm.rs`). Global
    slots are no longer all roots, and neither are all module objects.
    `Vm::collect` marks from the modules a name finds, and a file's or a
    scope's module is live while something reaches it: its object, a macro
    made in it, compiled code that names one of its slots (each template's
    `Global`, `SetGlobal`, `Define` and `Inline` slots), or a live module
    that uses it. Marking reports the modules and slots it reaches
    (`Heap::collect_with`, `Tracer::module`), until it reaches nothing new.
    A dead module's slots and index go on free lists that `cell` and
    `anonymous` use again. Its aliases and the expander's references into it
    are forgotten. The image records which modules are anonymous; a freed
    one has no object and a freed slot no owner, so a restore rebuilds the
    lists.
  - **`crates/core/examples/compile.rs`:** the corpus through `Engine`
    natively, one instance for every file, from a core image of the
    library's VM written in memory, writing `<name>.err` and
    `<name>.json`.

- **Built** (P7, 02 §6), in the parser's new `markup.rs`:
  - **Markup mode** by recursive descent over `parser.yy`'s `full_markup`,
    `full_markup_list`, `markup_mode_word` and the `markup_*` rules:
    words, braced lists, markup list commands, `markup_scm` (a `#` form or
    a `SCM_IDENTIFIER` as markup or a markup list by its value, the
    unspecified as an empty list, else `not a markup`), `\score` and
    `\score-lines` in markup (read in notes mode; their music is no
    toplevel score's).
  - **Commands by their signatures:** in markup mode the lexer looks a
    `\name` up as `name-markup`, then `name-markup-list`, in the innermost
    scope, as `lookup-markup-command` does, and so a `$` form whose value is
    a markup procedure; `markup-command-signature` gives the parameters.
    `(lily)`'s `%markup-procedure` (`lily.rs`) loads the part of a stub the
    name is bound to first: D74's trigger for the parts' commands, which
    step 13 left open. A command whose last parameter is `markup?` is a
    head, composed with what follows by `ly-syntax-constructors.scm`'s
    `composed-markup-list`, which `tests/support` now reads into `(lily)`
    (`DEFINITIONS`); any other is a markup of its own. A `scheme?` argument
    is a `#` form, a `SCM_IDENTIFIER`, a string, music, `\notemode`, or
    LilyPond in braces (nothing, a duration, music, a pitch alone), tried as
    the note it makes when its predicate rejects it
    (`make_music_from_simple`), as `parser.yy` does.
  - **Where markup goes:** toplevel and books (`toplevel-text-handler`'s,
    not called); scripts (`gen_text_def`: `\markup`, and a `#` form or a
    `SCM_IDENTIFIER` as `create-script` takes it, with `not an
    articulation`); music (`markup outside of text script or
    \lyricmode`); function arguments (the markup, else the lyric event it
    makes, else backed up or checked; `\markuplist` as Scheme);
    `identifier_init`; `scalar`; and `\markup name = …`, which defines the
    markup command with `define-markup-command-internal`, or is `Not a
    markup function`. `PostEventKind::Text` and `MusicKind::Lyric` hold a
    `syntax::Text`, a string or markup.
  - **Case 20's Guile abort (D64):** an argument its predicate rejects is
    `wrong type for argument N`, and leaves the command's arguments an
    improper list; the command's `scm_reverse_x` then throws, which
    escapes `ly:parse-file` and ends the run. The parser prints `ERROR: In
    procedure ly:parse-file:` and the error of the interpreter's
    `reverse!`, and no `failed files` or missing `\version` follow
    (`Parse::guile_abort`). The core's `diag.rs` reads the two lines into
    the error's message, as `parseStderr` does, with no change of code.
    The interpreter's `reverse!` now puts an improper list back and words
    its error as Guile's (`Wrong type argument in position 1: ("big" .
    #f)`, `lists.rs`).
  - **After a syntax error in markup** no rule pops the mode, so the rest
    of the file is lexed in markup mode, as LilyPond's lexer does
    (`markup_stuck`): P1's skeleton dropped the token, and `p2.rs`'s mk2
    now gives LilyPond's `not a note name: c4`, which that test had
    foretold for P7.

### MS2 · step 19 — Ask the host for included files and parts through lily_needs

- **Commits:** feat(engine): ask the host for included files and parts'
  files through lily_needs (D80).
- **Built** (D80):
  - **`\include "file"` in scores** (P11's string form, brought forward
    for T01, T03, T19 and T21): `source.rs`' `include_candidates` looks
    where LilyPond looks with `relative-includes` (checked on LilyPond
    2.26.0 by hand): beside the including file, then in the score's
    directory, then in `<datadir>/ly/`, an absolute name only itself;
    `cannot_find` is LilyPond's message with its search path, a
    directory of none printed as `.`. The lexer asks the scopes for each
    name (`Scopes::include_file`, now a `Hosted`), lexes the first the
    host has under that name, and ends the input on `Hosted::Ask` or when
    Scheme waits (`Scopes::waiting`, `Lexer::waiting`, `Parse::waiting`).
    `parse_including` gives a file's parse its include source;
    `parse_init`'s closure answers a `Hosted` too.
  - **A part source that can ask** (`lily.rs`): `PartSource` gives a
    `Hosted<String>`. On `Ask`, `%part-source` cancels the run, past every
    `catch`, and leaves the VM waiting (`Vm::waiting`, `Vm::take_waiting`).
    `%load-part!` asks for every file of its part before any of them runs
    (`%load-text`), so a part loads whole or not at all and a stopped load
    starts over on the next run.
  - **A part's own module loads the part when a file uses it**
    (`module.rs`' `%module-hooks`, run by `use-modules` and `#:use-module`
    through `%use-module!`, not by `resolve-module`). The image writer
    (`tests/support`' `part_module_hooks`) registers one for `display`'s
    `(lily display-lily)` and `qr`'s `(lily qr-code)` after the init, since
    `define-markup-commands.scm` uses `qr`'s at load. `articulate.ly` needs
    it: `display`'s `with-music-match` is a macro, which no stub stands
    for.
  - **The core** (`lib.rs`, `compile.rs`): the host's files are shared
    with the interpreter's part source, which asks for a part's file as
    `<datadir>/scm/lily/<file>`. A compile parses with `parse_including`.
    A parse that waited is dropped (the session ended, the output and the
    error port taken): the step returns 2 and `lily_needs` names the first
    file the parse lacked (kind 0); the next `lily_compile` or `lily_step`
    parses the root again from its start, with the answer. 08 §4.2's ABI
    and `packages/studio/src/web/engine/` are unchanged, so K2's stop point
    did not apply: the driver already starts a compile again after each
    answer.
  - **`init.ly`'s `(use-modules (srfi srfi-1))`** in a file's module
    (`Env::new`), used before the init files' modules, so that their
    variables come first as a file's own do in LilyPond: `\break` stays
    the init's music, not srfi-1's `break` (T12's tokens found it).
    `articulate.ly`'s `fold` needs it.
  - **`examples/compile.rs` answers from disk:** a name under
    `<datadir>/` from LilyPond's data directory (`--lily`'s `../..`), any
    other relative to the current directory, one not there put as none.

### MS2 · step 23 — Iterate music through the global loop

- **Commit:** feat(engine): iterate music through the global loop and
  trace it natively (N4, D84).
- **Built:**
  - **The iterators** (`crates/music/src/iterator.rs`, 04 §8): one enum
    in an arena of the translation's `Iteration`, numbered, with LilyPond's
    protocol (`create_children`, `init_context` and `create_contexts`,
    `pending_moment`, `ok`, `run_always`, `process`, `quit`) and its
    `get_context`/`set_context` (a wrapper's is its child's). Ported: the
    base iterator, simple music and its event, rhythmic and event chord
    kinds, sequential music (`look_ahead`, `pop_element`, grace time
    ahead), simultaneous music, the music wrapper, context-specced music
    (`create_new`, search directions, LilyPond's warnings at the music's
    origin) and initial-context music. `descend_to_bottom_context`,
    `descend_to_child` and `descend_to_user_accessible_context` find and
    make contexts through step 22's creation. An iterator holds its
    context as a `Context_handle` does, a client of it. A type's
    `iterator-ctor` names its iterator by D67's placeholder; music without
    one is an event's or simple; any other constructor's music is
    iterated as simple music, which keeps its time, and named in the
    translation's log. Music is read where it is: a frozen tree's nodes
    without thawing, live music through its handle; `SequentialMusic`'s
    elements natively, another type's `elements-callback` in Scheme, its
    list rooted till the translation ends. Lengths and starts are
    `length.rs`' natively, `ly:music-length` and `ly:music-start` where
    they need Scheme.
  - **Events refer to their music** (`dispatcher.rs`, D84): a
    `StreamEvent` holds the music, and its own properties are what
    `Music::to_event` adds (`class` from the type's name, `length`, the
    articulations as events, `music-cause`) with handles of music a frozen
    node holds; the music's mutable properties are read behind them. The
    rhythmic iterator broadcasts the articulations the context's event
    source listens to as events of their own, as LilyPond's does.
  - **The global loop** (`global.rs`): `Global_context::iterate` with
    `add_moment_to_process` and `sneaky_insert_extra_moment` (the arena's
    `add_moment`, `take_extra`), the first pass forced at 0, `Prepare`,

### MS2 · step 25 — Run translators through the timestep protocol

- **Commit:** feat(engine): run translators through the timestep protocol
  with Timing_translator; trace bars where LilyPond finds them (N5, D86).
- **Built:**
  - **Translator classes** (`crates/music/src/translator.rs`, 04 §9.1,
    D79): static Rust descriptions (`TranslatorClass`: name, engraver,
    performer or both, the protocol methods it has, whether they run every
    timestep, the event classes it hears and grob interfaces it
    acknowledges by name, `must_be_last`, the function that makes its
    state, `Work`). `CLASSES` holds LilyPond 2.26.0's 128 C++ classes:
    `Timing_translator` and 127 placeholders of chapters 05 and 07 (D67),
    named, with no work; `Axis_group_engraver` keeps `must_be_last`.
  - **Groups** (`Group`, one per context): made when the parent's group
    hears `AnnounceNewContext` (`create_child_translator`), Global's by
    `run_translator` (`connect_global`, `ly:make-global-translator`). The
    definition's `consists` after the context's `\with`, in LilyPond's
    order, filtered by output; a name looked up in the classes, then in
    what `ly:register-translator` keeps (a Scheme translator, held in its
    place for step 26), else LilyPond's `unknown translator` and `cannot
    find` warnings. Listeners go on the context's events below; an
    engraver group (the Score's too, as `Score_engraver` is one) hears the
    context's overrides and reverts, which step 24's `connect_group` gave
    only `Engraver_group`s; a Score's group hears Global's `Prepare`,
    `OneTimeStep` and `Finish` and runs the protocol over the tree as
    `Score_engraver` and `Score_performer` do (start down or up,
    pre-process and process up, the announcements, stop up, finalize
    children first). Removal disconnects a group's listeners.
  - **Wake lists:** a timestep's method is called on a translator whose
    class runs always, or that is awake: it heard an event, acknowledged a
    grob, or asked to stay awake in the timestep before (`Tx::stay_awake`).
    `initialize` and `finalize` run on every translator that has them. A
    method runs on its state taken out of the arena, its values rooted.
  - **Acknowledgers** (`Engraver_group::do_announces`): a grob announced to
    its group and each engraver group above; per group, grob name and
    start or end, the acknowledgers found once and kept; the maker
    skipped; `process_acknowledged` between passes until none is pending
    below. Performer groups tell their performers of audio items the same
    way (`Performer_group::do_announces`).
  - **Records** (`records.rs`): grob and audio records (name, origin,
    cause, moment, a grob's end and its interfaces as a 256-bit set,
    numbered per translation), what `Tx::make_grob`,
    `Tx::announce_end_grob` and `Tx::make_audio` make.
  - **`Timing_translator`** (`timing.rs`), ported whole: the `Timing`

  - **The trace** (`trace.rs`): `C` lines after the new group's

    A group's slots carry their methods and wake rule for classes and Scheme
    translators alike (`translator.rs`): a Scheme translator with a
    timestep method runs always, one of listeners only when they are
    called. Filtered by output, placed `must-be-last`, connected and
    disconnected as the classes are; its handle prints `#<Translator
    Scheme_engraver >`. `scheme-engravers.scm` runs in Scheme in every
    `\layout` translation.
  - **Grobs from Scheme:** `ly:engraver-make-grob` makes a grob record with
    the context's definition of the grob and its interfaces, announced to
    the groups above; its handle is `ly:grob?` (`#<Grob TextScript >`);
    `ly:engraver-announce-end-grob`, `ly:grob-property` and
    `ly:grob-set-property!` on it; a Scheme acknowledger gets the grob's
    handle and its maker's. `ly:breathing-sign::set-breath-properties`
    (`Breathing_sign_engraver`'s) is ported in Scheme. Stream events are
    `equal?` as `Prob::equal_p`, `origin` skipped, for `#:once` listeners.
  - **`format`:** a score's is `(ice-9 format)`'s, as Guile makes it once
    `lily.scm` loads that module, and `(lily)` keeps `simple-format`
    (`prims.rs`, `lily.rs`); T15's `~16a` needed it.
  - **The playback map** (`crates/music/src/playback.rs`, 04 §9.3, D26):
    `Lily_playback_performer`, `Lily_playback_staff_performer` and
    `Lily_playback_voice_performer`, built-in performers that a `\midi`
    translation (`run_performance`) gives the contexts whose definitions
    are named Score, Staff and Voice, where `timing.ly`'s `\consists` puts
    its own. They record `timing.ly`'s events (link, moment, grace, length,
    0 for a syllable), bars (where `currentBarNumber` changes) and staves
    (id, name, short name, group, clef, transposition, voices), and the
    Score's `finalize` writes the performance's JSON as `timing.ly` writes
    it.
  - **The core** (`compile.rs`): every compile translates each score's
    `\midi`, a score without one given `$defaultmidi` (and `$defaultlayout`
    before it if it has none) as `capture.ly` does, and writes
    `<name>.timing.json` through `lily_output` after `stderr` and
    `diagnostics.json`. What a performance says goes to no output. A file
    the score's Scheme writes is an output by its name, in place of the
    engine's of that name; `Engine::set_playback(false)` (the compile
    example's `--no-playback`) leaves the built-in performers out.
  - **What `timing.ly` needs** (`lily.rs`, `ports.rs`):
    `ly:string-percent-encode` (LilyPond's encoding, checked against
    2.26.0: `-./:_`, digits and letters kept, other bytes `%xx`),
    `ly:string-substitute`, `is-absolute?`, `ly-getcwd` (empty: the engine
    has no current directory), `ly:parser-output-name` (the root's base
    name, which the core sets), and `with-output-to-file` and
    `call-with-output-file` into `%written-files`.
  - **Sizes:** the N5 module row in `scripts/sizes.mjs` names
    `scheme_translator` and `playback` too.
- **Gate:**
  - **C1 = 1.0 on all 14 scores** (`tools/compare/test/c1.test.mjs`): the

### MS2 · step 30 — Ask for all of a part's files at the first stop

- **Commits:** five, one or two for each of the step's four sessions:

- **Built:**
  - **A compile's asked names are a queue** (D89; `crates/core`'s
    `Asked`, `hosted`): each name the parse lacks is queued once, in the
    order asked.
  - **`%part-sources`** (`crates/scheme/src/lily.rs`): `%load-part!`
    gives it the part's files not loaded yet, and it asks the host for
    every one it lacks before cancelling the run, where `%part-source`
    stopped at the first. A stub's call (D76) and a part's module (D80)
    both load a part through it. `%part-source` stays for
    `%load-source`.
  - **`Engine::step` goes through the queue** (`compile.rs`): after a
    stop it returns `NEEDS` for each queued name the host has not put,
    one per `lily_needs`, with no parse between them, and parses again
    once they are all put. **`Engine::compile` takes the revision:** the
    same revision and root, as a host starts the compile again after each
    answer, keep the queue; another drops it. `lily_compile` passes the
    revision it was always given (08 §4.2's signature unchanged).
  - **`Engine::parses`, exported as `lsb_parses`** beside `lsb_times`:
    how many times the compile parsed its root.
  - **The hosts** (`examples/compile.rs`, `tools/compare/core.mjs`):
    each name answered as asked and the compile started again with the
    same revision, as the studio's driver does; both count the stops (a
    name asked after another parse), `compileInWasm` giving each file's
    `stops` and `parses`, `--time` printing the stops after the names
    asked (the time columns move one to the right).

### MS2 · step 32 — Parse lyrics: \addlyrics, \lyrics and the syllables

- **Commits:** c88bb60 feat(engine): parse lyrics (the code and its
  tests), and the one that adds D91 and this entry.
- **Built:**
  - **Lyrics mode is a music mode of D82's stack** (D91; `chord.rs`,
    `notes.rs`): `\lyricmode` and `\lyrics` are heads of
    `mode_changed_music`, `\lyrics` making `\new Lyrics` with its
    `\with`s; `lyric_mode_music` after `\addlyrics` and `\lyricsto`
    pushes the mode once the token after them is lexed (`{`, `<<`,
    `\sequential`, `\simultaneous`, or a `MUSIC_IDENTIFIER`, which takes
    none), and a token that starts none is LilyPond's syntax error with
    the mode left pushed. The lists of lyrics mode are `music_list`, so
    `\set`, `\override`, `\skip`, braces, `<< >>` and function calls are
    read there; part 2's list of syllables is gone.
  - **Syllables** (`lyric_element_music`): words, strings, `\markup`,
    and Scheme markup (`music_embedded_backup BACKUP`), with durations,
    dots and multipliers (`optional_notemode_duration`) and any
    post-events, `--` and `__` among them (`HYPHEN` and `EXTENDER` are
    post-events now, "have to be in Lyric mode for lyrics" outside it);
    a string's syllable placed at its closing quote, as `@1` of a
    `STRING` is; a word of lyrics mode its text with `_` as spaces

- **Built:**
  - **The interpreter calls its host from a primitive** (D92; `vm.rs`,
    `lily.rs`, `control.rs`): `(%host-call what arg …)` returns to the
    loop, which calls the host's function (`Vm::set_host`) with the
    whole VM and the arguments, still on the stack; a run it leaves
    waiting cancels the caller's. `Vm::apply` was reentrant already.
  - **Templates by `parser-ly-from-scheme.scm` as it is** (`embedded.rs`,
    new): `ly:parser-clone`, `ly:parse-string-expression`,
    `ly:parser-parse-string`, `ly:parser-has-error?` and
    `ly:parser-clear-error`, Scheme in `(lily)` with LilyPond's argument
    checks over `%host-call`. Each parse publishes a `Lily_parser` value
    as `(lily)`'s `%parser` (`classify.rs`' `Env`): its scopes, pitch
    names and language, default duration and tremolo, and its error,
    which a clone copies with its closures and location. A template's
    text is parsed at each call from the synthetic `EMBEDDED_LILY` as
    `embedded_lilypond` (nothing, a duration, a number, post-events, one
    item as an assignment's value, a pitch alone a pitch, or a music
    list), its lines numbered from its `#{`'s (`Source::with_line`), its
    source numbered apart from the running parse's files; a `#` or `$`
    form at a byte of the closures is read for its end and its closure
    called in its place; its music placed at the call (`override_input`).
    A syntax error after a whole item keeps the item and aborts, as
    Bison's default reduction of `start_symbol` does; one in a list is
    `music_list error`'s.

    path =`, `\set path =` and `\repeat kind [count]`, a call's last
    argument), a music, event or Scheme function's call, those property
    operations, `\repeat` and a direction are read with `etc`: their
    arguments one at a time (`args.rs`' `arguments_etc`, `function.rs`'
    `call`), an `\etc` where an argument is due ending them, not taken,

    `repeat.rs`' `repeated_music_etc`, `notes.rs`' `script_done`). Each
    call is Bison's `(function . arguments)`, last first, `#f`-ended after
    a rejected argument; `partial_function ETC` hands them to
    `partial-music-function`, a direction first to
    `create-script-function`. A template that begins with a music
    function, `\override`, `\set` or `\repeat` is read so too
    (`embedded.rs`).

### MS2 · step 36 — Iterate \change and parse T25's assignments

- **Commits:** 96a6fca feat(engine): iterate \change and parse T25's

- **Built:**
  - **The change iterator** (`iterator.rs`, `change-iterator.cc`, D95): a
    kind of N4's simple iterator (`Simple::Change`). Processed, it finds
    the context of the music's `change-to-type` above its own and the one
    of that type and `change-to-id` near it; then, over each iterator of
    its scope in preorder, takes an iterator held by the first to the
    second (`substitute_context`), or moves the branch below the first to
    the second by a `ChangeParent` event at the music's origin, which the
    context hears as it has since step 22 (`change_parent`). LilyPond's
    warnings when either context is missing: `cannot find context to
    change from: Type`, `… to: Type = id`.
  - **Iterators know their parents** (`parent_`), so the scope is
    `where_tagged`'s (a `change-tag` symbol, held by the nearest `tags` of
    an iterator's music or its ancestors', else the change iterator
    itself), and `preorder_walk` goes down a sequence's current element,
    a simultaneous music's children and a wrapper's child.
  - **`find_context (CENTER)` made whole** (`context.rs`): the arena's
    stopped after the searches below and above; `unchecked_find` then
    walks down from each context above, which is how `\change Staff =
    two` from inside staff one finds its sibling. Nothing asked for
    `CENTER` before.
  - **T25's grammar** (`assign.rs`): `identifier_init` takes
    `context_change` (`music_assign`'s `simple_music`), defined before
    the token after it is lexed, as LilyPond 2.26.0 does (`probe/peek*.ly`:
    a `\csh` on the next line is known; `x = { c }` then `\x` is not).
    T25's `_\tweak X-offset #1 -\appassmolto` needed nothing: steps

### MS2 · step 37 — Iterate volta repeats and alternatives

- **Commits:** 49df90d feat(engine): iterate volta repeats and

- **Built:**
  - **The volta repeat iterator** (`iterator.rs`,
    `volta-repeat-iterator.cc`, `repeat-styler.cc`, D96): a kind of N4's
    sequence (`SeqKind::Repeat`) owning its repeat styler, volta or segno
    by its music's type, null inside `lyric-combine-music`. The first time
    it is processed it reports its start with the span of its time
    (`VoltaRepeatStartEvent`, or a segno mark), and once it has ended its
    return (`VoltaRepeatEndEvent`, `DalSegnoEvent`) unless its
    alternatives reported one. Its elements are `make-volta-set`'s, as
    before.
  - **The alternative sequence iterator**
    (`alternative-sequence-iterator.cc`): a sequence (`SeqKind::Alternatives`)
    using the styler of the nearest folded repeat above. The first time:
    the alternatives' alignment with the repeat, each one's returns,
    whether they are in order, LilyPond's `missing volta specification on
    alternative element`; the styler's brackets and their depth (an
    enclosing `\alternative`'s added); `alternativeRestores` saved where
    defined when `timing` is on; the first alternative's start
    (`AlternativeEvent`, or a coda mark). After each element: the ended
    alternative's returns, the group's end after the last, the saved
    properties restored after each but the last (`measurePosition` at the
    alternative's grace time), the next one's start.
  - **The volta-specced music iterator**
    (`volta-specced-music-iterator.cc`): a wrapper (`Wrap::Volta`) that, as
    a child of an `\alternative` with brackets, sends `VoltaSpanEvent`
    start and stop to the context it started in, held as a client.
    `\volta n` in `\alternative` and in a body needed nothing more.

### MS2 · step 38 — Combine lyrics with their voices

- **Commits:** d8f25f1 feat(engine): combine lyrics with their voices (MS2
  step 38) (the code and its tests), and the one that adds D97 and this
  entry.
- **Built:**
  - **The lyric combine iterator** (`iterator.rs`,
    `lyric-combine-music-iterator.cc`, D97): `\lyricsto` and `\addlyrics`
    (`LyricCombineMusic`), a kind of N4's arena (`Kind::Combine`) holding
    its lyrics' iterator. Its pending moment is never finite; it runs
    always while its lyrics last and the voice cannot be removed. Its
    contexts made: the `Lyrics` context at or below its lyrics' own
    (LilyPond's `argument of \lyricsto should contain Lyrics context`),
    the voice of `associatedVoice` and `associatedVoiceType`, or of
    `\lyricsto`'s id and type, below Global. Each timestep it looks for
    the voice again; when the voice heard a melodic event now it sets the
    lyrics' `associatedVoiceContext` and processes its lyrics' iterator
    to that iterator's next moment, one syllable; a grace note's syllable
    waits for its main note unless `includeGraceNotes`. At `quit`,
    LilyPond's `cannot find context: Voice = id` if it never found the
    voice. It takes part in `preorder_walk` and has its own
    `substitute_context` (D95's Open item).
  - **Its listeners** (`lyrics.rs`, new; `Listener::Combine` in
    `dispatcher.rs`, `Arena::combines` in `context.rs`, D97): `set_busy`
    (the voice's last `melodic-event`), `forward_event` (the voice's
    `structural-event`s sent on to the lyrics' context: the repeats and
    alternatives inside `\lyricsto`, step 37's Open item) and
    `check_new_context` (the voice looked for at each `CreateContext`),
    their state in the translation's arena, since a dispatch cannot reach
    the iterators.
  - **An iterator's `quit` takes the host** (`iterator.rs`, `global.rs`),
    for `do_quit`'s warning.
  - **`melisma_busy` is not ported** (step 39): no melisma holds a
    syllable back, and each line that changes is recorded below.
  - **Tests' lists** (`trace.mjs`, D97): `TRACED` gains T20 (the 25).
  - **A fixture** (`tools/compare/fixtures/lyrics.ly`), one score with no
    melisma: a rest, a grace note with and without `includeGraceNotes`, a
    voice made at 1/2, `associatedVoice` switched, a volta repeat with
    alternatives, a voice moved by `\change`, two `\addlyrics`, `\lyricsto`
    of a voice that never comes and of music without `Lyrics`.
  - `scripts/sizes.mjs`: an *N7: lyrics* module row.
- **Tests:** in `packages/engine`, after `npm run build`, with nothing

- **Built:**
  - **`melisma_busy`** (`melisma.rs`, new; `context.cc`, D98): a context
    with children is held if all of them are, one without if any property
    of `melismaBusyProperties` is `#t` there. The lyric combine iterator's
    `start_new_syllable` (`lyrics.rs`) asks it of the voice it follows
    unless the lyrics' `ignoreMelismata` is set, so a melisma holds a
    syllable back (step 38's Open item).

    properties** (`melisma.rs`, `translator.rs`' `CLASSES`):
    `Slur_engraver` (the spanner ids of its open slurs, from `slur-event`s
    on their own or a chord's note's articulations; `slurMelismaBusy` in
    every `process_music`), `Beam_engraver` and `Grace_beam_engraver`
    (whether their beam is open, in main or grace time;
    `beamMelismaBusy` only with `autoBeaming` off), `Slur_performer` and
    `Beam_performer` (the last start and stop heard now), `Tie_engraver`
    and `Tie_performer` (the notes waiting for the notes they are tied to,
    with their ends; `tieMelismaBusy` at each timestep's start and when a
    tie is heard; a note past its end forgotten unless `tieWaitForNote`).
    Their grobs, audio and warnings stay chapter 05's and 07's.

    the context consists such a maker, and takes each note as its head or
    audio note: tied to the first waiting note of an `equal?` pitch, else
    of the same tones; its end its length later, for an audio note after
    each articulation's `midi-length` (a staccato's), called as
    `Note_performer` calls it.
