### The plan

**What MS6 builds, counted.** MS6 ports no LilyPond file: its code is the
chapters' designs. The counts were made for the split from the chapters,
the 30 references and the engine's tree at 8ca7c5a; the scripts and their
output are in `$LILY_CORPUS/ms6-split/` (not a repository), whose
`README.md` names each; `all.sh` makes every count again: 34 checks, all
agree, and two runs give the same files byte for byte.

- **The design each piece implements** (`design.txt`: non-blank lines of
  the chapters' sections and step rows): 307 lines. The harness 21 (00
  §6.2, 05 §6.3); S5 21 (only what S5 turns on: 03 §5.1's epochs, §5.4's
  slots, 02 §5.8's two demands, R10 and R11; S1–S3 built the heap and the
  slots); the re-parse 40 (02 §5.7); N8's checkpoints 26 (04 §10.1–10.2,
  N8's row), convergence and the change list 17 (§10.5–10.6), partitions
  21 (§10.3), the run and replay 32 (§10.4, §10.7); Y7's cells 40 (05
  §6.1–6.2, Y7's row), the DPs and the queue 37 (05 §7); W4 and W8 28 (06
  §6.3–6.4, their rows); H3 24 (08 §4.3, 09 §4.5).
- **What the engine has of it** (`engine.txt`, at 8ca7c5a, 133,310
  non-blank lines in `crates/*/src`): S1's epochs per chunk
  (`heap.rs`: the write barrier named, not on), S3's slot versions
  (`module.rs`' `versions`, R10's beside them), N2's digests of frozen
  music (`frozen.rs`), C2.2's options reset after each compile (MS4 step
  14); the compile is one step (`compile.rs`: "Parses the root in one
  step"), from scratch each time. **It lacks** checkpoints, an undo log
  and `data-lily-cell` (no hit in `crates/*/src`). Each step's files and
  their lines now are listed there; the new ones are `parser/src/reuse.rs`,
  `music/src/checkpoint.rs` and `partition.rs`, `layout/src/cell.rs` and
  `queue.rs`, and the tests and tools beside them.
- **Cells** (`cells.txt`: a VerticalAxisGroup's copy in a system of

**Why this order.**

- **The harness first (1)**, by answer 2 and README's R5: every later step
  is judged by it, and it must be shown to see a difference before any
  reuse can hide one. Until a layer is incremental its "incremental"
  compile is from scratch, so each step's own layers turn incremental
  under a test that already passes for the others.
- **S5 before the re-parse (2–3)**: 02 §5.7's step 2 undoes the old items'
  effects with their undo logs, and its step 4 needs every global's
  version (03's R10, R11). `ly:set-option`'s persistence (C2.2) is an
  effect of an item on state older than it, the undo log's case.
- **N8 after the re-parse (4–7)**: its "what changed" is the parse's
  changed items and the music's digests (04 §10.1); checkpoints and
  convergence (4–5) are enough for the S scores and pitch edits (04 §10.7
  (a)); partitions (6–7) are what bring a reflow in an L score under
  budget ((b): T29 131 → 16–41 ms), so they come second, with T24's
  reflow (R1's translation half) last.
- **Y7 after N8 (8–9)**: layout reads N8's change list (04 §10.6, 05
  §6.2); the cells and their keys first, then the DPs and the queue that
  order them, with T29's reflow (R1's layout half) last.
- **W4 and W8 after Y7 (10)**: a cell is Y7's unit; the writer keeps its
  markup per cell and the preview replaces cells by digest (06 §6.3–6.4).
- **H3 last of the code (11)**: the engine returns between systems once
  the queue (9) has them as its steps; B8 and memory then measure the whole
  path. The gate (12) needs everything, the close (13) the gate.

about 2,520 and 3,110 at twice their tops; cut as 04 §10 divides them,

  (PLANS.md R7; the reset after each compile is MS4 step 14's): an
  option an item sets is undone with the item.
- **3**: F's three include gaps: an `\include` read again in the incl
  state, an `\include` in a template (D92), the include search asking its
  candidates at one stop.
- **7**: R1's translation half (README §8: T24's reflow, 106 ms against
  100 projected).
- **9**: R1's layout half (T29's reflow, 650 ms against 480 projected).
- **10**: E11 (W4, the preview form and cells).
- **11**: B8 with a 26-page score (T29 × 26).
- **12**: B6 and its decision point; D1's misses and D8 measured again
  (answer 6); D88 on the devices.
- **3, 7, 9, 11** (the parts' closes) and **13**: C1, D1, D2, D7, E4, E10,
  E13, H4 recorded.
- **Not R7's**: R8's (D4, D5, E14, E15, E17, E22, G3, H2, I1, I3) and R9's
  (C2's and F's others, C3, C4, E5, A25, A28), as OPEN.md places them.

**Decisions.** The split takes two, from the operator's answers: **D232**
(W8's message and the preview's handling in R7, answer 3) and **D233** (B6
read on the iPhone and the emulator, the Android tablet beside;
the devices at MS6's gate and close; answer 5), in docs/DECISIONS.md.
**The next free D-numbers are D234 (the engine) and D170 (the apps).**

**Stop points of MS6**, beside the runway's (PROTOCOL §6). A step that
reaches one stops and asks (PLAN-RUN §3):

- **B6's decision point** (step 12; README §5, IMPLEMENT's *Limits*): the
  figures phase by phase on the iPhone and the emulator against §4.3,
  reported with the leads; the user decides. Not re-planned on it alone.
- **A difference the harness finds with no cause** (every step from 2):
  an incremental compile that differs from one from scratch in any layer,
  after the step's fixes, stops; it is never passed by a tolerance or by
  turning a reuse off without saying so.
- **The harness itself** (step 1): a layer in which a planted difference
  is not caught stops before step 2.
- **Module boundaries** (PROTOCOL §6.2): the music crate naming a layout
  type (the change list goes to layout through the core); a crate beyond
  today's; the core growing beyond the calls behind 08 §4.2's ABI.
  `protocol.ts`, `driver.ts`, `host.ts` or a studio test changing stops,
  except step 10's within D232.
- **An output that changes where a step says none does** (every step):
  from-scratch compiles of the 30, M01–M12 and every fixture stay byte for
  byte (`grobs.tsv`, `layout.tsv`, pages, traces, stderr, playback maps,
  MIDI files); a reference of `ref/` changing stops (§6.4).
- **A function of no part** (§6.3): a placeholder or a LilyPond function
  an incremental path reaches that no step ports.
- **Size of a change** (§6.7): past 2,500 lines at twice the top, the step
  builds the part that fits and asks where the rest goes.
- **The budgets**: a per-edit phase, B8 or memory over twice its Must at a
  part's close with no lead; B6's translation phase over Must after N8 (D8,
  answer 6), at step 12.
- **The devices** (12, 13; answer 5): the operator attaches the Android
  tablet (unlocked, Silk in front: `svc power stayon true`, `cpuset`
  `/top-app`, `stayon` back to `false` after) and the iPhone
  (over trusted HTTPS) on asking; the scripts copied from the latest dated
  run under `$LILY_CORPUS/device-runs/` into a new dated folder; a device
  that cannot be reached stops before deciding on the emulator alone.
- **D88 at the close**: a miss over twice on the iPhone or the emulator is
  listed with its lead; one whose lead the measurements do not name stops.

### MS6 · step 2 — Turn on S5's write barrier and undo log

- **Commits:** one, on 2d7f873 (step 1's, pushed): `crates/scheme`

  `tests/engine.rs`, `tools/compare/test/differential.test.mjs` (KNOWN

  runway/LEDGER.md and this entry. One session; its handoff is on the chunk

- **The handoff agreed:** step 1's entry's *Next* names this step; LEDGER.md's
  next action still named step 1 (step 1's session left it), now step 3.
- **Built:**
  - **The heap's write barrier and undo log** (R11, 03 §5.1): while an item
    runs (`Heap::begin_item`, a new epoch), the first change in it of each
    object older than the item is logged with what the object was: a
    pair's car and cdr, a string's text, a vector's items, a foreign
    object's `Foreign::snapshot` (hash tables, weak ones too, fluids,
    promises, GOOPS instances, arrays; ports and the other crates' types
    give none). The barrier is in the five accessors every change goes
    through (`set_car`, `set_cdr`, `str_mut`, `vector_items_mut`,
    `foreign_mut`), so `set-car!`, `vector-set!`, `vector-fill!`,
    `string-set!`, `hash-set!` and their kin, `set-object-property!`,
    `fluid-set!`, `force`, `array-set!` and a closure's boxed `set!` are
    all logged. `Heap::undo` gives them back, the latest first. The log's
    objects and what it holds are roots, a weak table's copy pruned as the
    table is, so no sweep frees a slot the log writes to.
  - **The slots' half** (R10, R11, 03 §5.4): the first `define`, `set!`,
    `module-define!`, `module-set!` or `export` of a slot in an item logs its
    value and flags; undone, the slot gets them back with a version it never
    had. Reads are recorded with the version of their first read. The
    logged slots' modules are kept by the collector.
  - **`Vm::begin_item` / `end_item` / `undo`**: an `Item` gives its
    `Mark`, its reads with versions and its writes in order (02 §5.7's
    dependencies and effects for step 3); the barrier is off outside items.
  - **A part's load is not logged** (`%undo-suspend!`, `%undo-resume!`
    around `%load-part!`'s body): it stays loaded after an undo, as before,
    in a new epoch after it (D234).
  - **The core** (D234): a compile is one item from its parse to its last
    output, undone when it ends and at each of its three stops (a file, a
    part's files, font packs), before `session-terminate` and
    `ly:reset-all-fonts`, which stay for what the log does not reach.
- **Settled:** **OPEN C7** (T27's `string-1-5`): the stopped parse's
  `color-table` entry is undone, so the from-scratch compile warns
  `Requested color 'purpole' is not defined!` as LilyPond and the
  incremental compile do (both `.err` checked); KNOWN is empty. **C2.2's

MS7 is README §5's *In Lily Studio on the web*, the integration of 08 §7: K5
(`Cache-Control` in D55's gateway, `persist()` after use, the debug build), K6
(`engine.js`, live preview in the page, the server's live compiles off while the
engine runs, the server as fallback for every compile the engine fails or cannot
do), M7 (the performance after the page, cancellable, Export MIDI from the engine's
bytes), K7 (00 §6's full measurement on the devices) and H2/D58's port to
`ScorePreview`. **The engine starts shipping here.** It is the runway's plan **R8**
(runway/PLANS.md R8), in `.worktrees/engine` on `feat/engine`. By D256 it first takes
what MS6 left: translation's cost per edit, the 26-page score, layout per edit, what
a newer edit waits on, and room in B1. MS7 runs in four parts; its split (MS7 · step
0) writes *The plan* and every step line at once; its steps are 1–11, step 11 its
close.

**Gate (README §5, MS7, as D257 reads it):** D55's tests pass with the engine and with
the engine refused; the page is driven end to end with the engine in Chromium and
WebKit; a second visit downloads only the manifest; rendering goes on when the
network drops. **Hard, holding the default (D257):** no trap (a score over the cap a
diagnostic); no killed tab on the Android floor's stand-in; B8 and B7 within Must;
the fallback working. **Measured and recorded:** B1–B6 on the iOS and Android
references, a miss over twice stopping at step 10 (D88); B4 on the stand-in. With every
earlier gate (MS6's differential, MS4's C3–C5 on the 30 with only triggered modules,
MS5's C2 on the 42, MS3's on the 10, MS2's C1 on the 30).

the trap before the page can meet one (a hard item). Layout (3) and the longest steps
(4) follow on the same measurements, since what remains of B6 is theirs once translation
is cut, and B24's stopped compile is cheapest after 1's resume. Step 5 comes before the
page because the page's first visit is what K5 caches, and the site's licences go with the
files they describe. The page is then built behind `?engine=1` (6), made safe to use with
the fallback (7), given playback (8), and only then made the default (9), with H2's port
before the switch so that the first default page is D58's. The devices (10) measure the
default, and the close (11) reads every gate on it.

  first if the hard items are to hold.

### Device runs, by hand

1. **The Android tablet** (10:33–12:40), **the Android e-reader** (17:53–19:01) and **the iPhone** (18:10–19:03),
   each left as found: the tablet's stayon false, the e-reader's stayon true and its screensaver on, no tunnels, `tailscale
   serve` as found, every harness server stopped. **On the iPhone, the run's Safari tab and the site data of
   `<mac>.<tailnet>.ts.net:8470` are the operator's to clear** (Settings › Safari › Advanced › Website Data),
   and Auto-Lock back to its setting.
2. **The A15-class Android phone:** never run (OPEN D4, past the runway).

### The grand plan's end

**R9's close is the grand plan's last step** (runway/GRAND-PLAN.md, *Done*): R2 to R9 have run in order, each closed by
its closing step, R9 with MS8's gate passed. The engine compiles every score of the corpus and the 90 regression scores
as LilyPond 2.26.0 does, natively and in `core.wasm`, re-renders only what an edit changes, runs in Lily Studio on the web
behind `?engine=1` with the server as its fallback, plays its MIDI and exports its PDFs. **The grand plan's *Done when* is
met but for the default** (answer 4 at R9's split: it cannot be met as written while the source is private), which waits on
the source and on B7 on Android T29. After the runway: R10's LilyPond 2.28 upgrade (README §8) and OPEN.md's items carried
past it.

### The plan

**What MS8 builds, counted.** The scripts and their output are in `$LILY_CORPUS/ms8-split/` (not a repository), whose
`README.md` names each; `all.sh` makes every count again (**42 checks, all agree, two runs byte for byte**). Read against
LilyPond 2.26.0's sources, the 30 references, the engine's tree at 2125e2b and the docs.

- **Y8** (`census.txt`): **none of Y8's first five nor ancient notation is reached by the 30.** Of the five, **KeyCancellation
  and PhrasingSlur are made and drawn by the engine already** (`key_engraver.rs`, MS3; `phrasing_slur_engraver.rs`, MS4 step
  7) and need only their regression scores; **TextMark** is the image's Scheme engraver (`Text_mark_engraver`) with callbacks
  the engine has; **RehearsalMark lacks `Mark_engraver`; RepeatTie and its column lack `Repeat_tie_engraver`.** Custos is the
  image's Scheme engraver; the three ligatures' `::print` are D67's placeholders. **Of the 83 grob types no score reaches, 33
  are wholly the engine's and 50 lack a maker or a callback:** 3 of the five, 5 of ancient notation's, and **Y8's rest, 42
  grobs beyond them** (pedals, percent and slash repeats, trills' pitches, ambitus, clusters, cue clefs, caesuras, parentheses,
  coda and segno marks, section labels, jumps, balloons, footnotes, grid lines, measure spanners, note names, the part
  combiner's texts, melody items, vowel transitions), held back by 30 `lily/*.cc` files (`rest-files.txt`). README puts all
  of Y8 in MS8, so they have steps 7 and 8.
- **The LilyPond lines left** (`lines.txt`, less what the engine cites, defines or has as a ported class): **10,125**: step 7
  2,338, step 8 3,124, step 9 4,389 (the ligatures 3,199, the page breakers 1,190), step 10 274. **29 classes are new**
  (`Mark_engraver`, `Repeat_tie_engraver`, the ligature engravers, `Page_turn_engraver`, `Quote_iterator` and the rest's 19).
- **The iterators: three of README's four are the engine's** (the part combiner at MS5 step 6a, percent repeats and `\fine`
  at MS5 step 6); **only `Quote_iterator` is left** (274 lines), with OPEN C4's `\fine` event to read again: the music crate
  names a `fine-event` now.
- **S6** (`scheme.txt`): **03 §6's seven parts are all built as modules** (MS7 step 7, I2); `modal` and `qr` are reached by no
  score or fixture, so step 11 gives each a regression score. **`syntax-case` is refused by the expander** (D60), used by four
  `scm/lily` files (`accreg`, `curried-definitions`, `lily-library`, `music-functions`, each with native stand-ins); 03 §4.2's
  20–35 KB raw at the core's 20.1 bytes a line is 995–1,741 lines.
- **W7** (`pdf.txt`): **LilyPond's PDFs made again here**: T02 56,532 bytes (2 pages; C059 Roman and Bold, Emmentaler-20), T20

runs run 2's size. T29's parse and a page's rendering (2) are the hard items the default failed; the soundness items (3) are
what the default waits on beside them; I7 and the gaps (4) close part 1 on what the page shows. With the source private the
flag is not turned (answer 4): part 1 still makes the engine fit to be the default, so that the operator's later yes needs
only the switch. W7 (5) needs only the display list (06 §9) and its licence check, and Export PDF (6) builds on it. Y8 goes by
how common a grob is in real scores (README §5): the five and the marks and repeats (7), the other common grobs (8), then
ancient notation and the page breakers (9). The quote iterator, `\fine` and P12 (10) and S6's rest, `syntax-case` and the
inherited tail (11) touch the parser and translation, after layout's long tail has its scores. The close (12) reads every gate.
